title: Postmortem & Action Plan: quantization-induced accuracy drift and runtime crash loop
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During the 2026-03-10 rollout of runtime-1.22 we enabled a new aggressive quantization profile (auto-quant-4bit) for several open models to reduce token cost. Within ~45 minutes some model shards entered a kernel crash loop on our GPU pool and others produced silent accuracy drift (coherent hallucinations and token-level distribution shifts) causing client errors and degraded quality for 3 enterprise customers and multiple self-serve integrations.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC: Canary of auto-quant-4bit profile started for model-family/llama-2-13b on dedicated-hosting pool A.
- 2026-03-10 09:47 UTC: First kernel crash observed from pool A; autoscaler attempted to restart pods.
- 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC: Crash loops escalate; requests got routed to fallback CPU variant via smart routing, causing latency spikes and request timeouts.
- 2026-03-10 10:20 UTC: Ops pager; mitigation: temporary rollback of auto-quant-4bit profile at 10:36 UTC (runtime-1.22 flag toggled).
- 2026-03-10 11:05 UTC: Metrics show quality regressions persisted for models previously quantized (accuracy delta still present).

Impact:
- Availability: 3 enterprise customers on Dedicated experienced degraded throughput & elevated tail latency (20–50% increase in p99). Several self-serve customers observed hallucination/accuracy issues (estimated 0.6% of total request volume during incident window).
- Economics: Hardware autoscaler churn increased spot usage and force-billed restarts; estimated incremental cost for the incident ~ $24k.
- Reliability: Two GPU nodes required manual recovery due to repeated driver/kernel restarts.

Root cause (summary):
Multiple contributing factors produced the outage and regression: 
1) Quantization incompatibility: The new auto-quant-4bit transformation path introduced an unsupported fused op pattern for certain Llama-derived kernels. When the runtime selected an optimized CUDA kernel, the kernel did not handle a rare attention-padding pattern, causing illegal memory access and crash loops.
2) Silent numeric drift: For a subset of operator chains the 4-bit lowering produced higher rounding accumulation than our tests covered, creating subtle distribution shifts in logits that manifested as accuracy drift on regression prompts.
3) Canary scope mismatch: Canary was run on a limited traffic slice that did not include the production sequence length distribution for some customers; we missed edge-case ops.
4) Model pin/rollout bug: Rollout controller allowed partial deployment to dedicated pools without pinning model artifact checksums, permitting mixed runtime variants and creating path-dependent failures.
5) Observability gap: No metric was tracking op-compatibility failure rate or quantized-fallback occurrences; the first signal was kernel crash logs rather than an aggregate KPI.

Immediate mitigations applied during incident:
- Rolled back auto-quant-4bit flag across all pools at 2026-03-10 10:36 UTC (rollback confirmed 10:42 UTC).
- Manual restart and GPU node drain/reprovision for two affected nodes.
- Temporary routing rule added to avoid the affected GPU pool until verification completed.
- Notified impacted customers and opened support cases; provided temporary model-version pin guidance.

Longer-term corrective actions (proposed & owners):
1) Add pre-deploy model compatibility check (binary op graph compatibility) that simulates supported kernel patterns and rejects quantization profiles that produce unsupported fused ops. Owner: Claire Nguyen. Due: 2026-03-21.
2) Expand regression test harness to include production sequence-length distributions (autogen from recent requests) and targeted numeric-sensitivity tests for logits. Owner: Ravi Shah. Due: 2026-03-18.
3) Implement a quantization-canary policy that enforces gradual traffic ramp with blocklist for pools lacking validated kernel support; require artifact checksum pin before full rollout. Owner: Miguel Santos. Due: 2026-03-24.
4) Create 'quantization-compatibility' metrics (op_compatibility_ratio, quantized_success_rate, kernel_crash_rate) and add alert thresholds to SRE runbooks. Owner: Noah Becker. Due: 2026-03-17.
5) Introduce circuit-breaker for aggressive fallback: if a quantized variant causes >X crash/sec or >Y format-mismatch errors in a 5m window, automatically disable quantized path for that model family and notify oncall. Owner: Elena Rodriguez. Due: 2026-03-20.
6) Post-release safety flag: require manual sign-off for any quantization profile that changes lowering passes for model families used by enterprise customers. Owner: Sofia Li (Product). Due: 2026-03-25.
7) Patch runtime kernel check: make kernel selection verify op preconditions at load-time and fall back to safe kernel instead of crashing on unsupported conditions. Owner: Claire Nguyen. Due: 2026-03-28.
8) Customer remediation: reach out to affected customers with detailed incident report and offer assisted revalidation of their pinned models. Owner: Miguel Santos (Customer Ops). Due: 2026-03-16.

Action items (trello-style list with status):
- [ ] Pre-deploy op-compat check (Claire Nguyen) — blocked by spec for fused-op signatures (tracked in ENG-4888).
- [ ] Regression harness updates (Ravi Shah) — in progress; added 12 new sequence-length fixtures.
- [ ] Canary policy implementation (Miguel Santos) — in progress; initial canary gating PR submitted. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7412
- [ ] Observability metrics + alerts (Noah Becker) — planned; dashboard draft at https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/quant-compat
- [ ] Automatic circuit-breaker (Elena Rodriguez) — planned; design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/QUANT-CB
- [ ] Runtime kernel guard (Claire Nguyen) — planned; low-level patch branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/quant-kernel-guard

Notes about testing and verification:
- Verify fixes using a seeded replay environment derived from the incident window; provide golden prompt sets used to detect accuracy drift.
- Add model-level integration tests that run quantize -> lower -> kernel-simulate -> E2E inference to detect illegal memory patterns.

Postmortem communications plan:
- Draft incident report published to ops-incident channel and customer-facing summary prepared for impacted enterprise accounts (owner: Miguel Santos).
- Follow-up doc will be posted in Confluence with deep-dive kernel traces and PR links.
